findings.summary: The local linkedom DOM adapter types duplicate the sanitizer module's DOM adapter types.
findings.consequence: Future sanitizer/parser changes must update the same structural DOM surface in multiple files, so a later change can silently type-check in one module while leaving the other with a stale parseHTML cast shape.
findings.evidence: The owned module declares SanitizableAttribute/SanitizableParent/SanitizableNode/SanitizableElement/ParsedDocument at lines 26-49. server/utils/reader-source-info-sanitizer.ts declares the same structural Sanitizable* and ParsedDocument types at lines 15-38, and rg shows the same pattern repeated in other server parsing utilities.
findings.recommendation: Extract the shared minimal linkedom adapter types to a small server utility type module, or import the sanitizer-owned adapter type if that module is made the common HTML boundary, so parser shape changes are made once.
verification: Inspected owned physical lines in server/utils/reader-source-info-projection.ts with nl -ba, plus surrounding projection functions for behavior context.

Inspected direct imports: server/utils/reader-source-info-definitions.ts, server/utils/reader-source-info-sanitizer.ts, server/utils/reader-source-info-validation.ts, shared/types/reader-source-info.ts, and shared/types/renderable-html.ts.
Inspected direct caller server/utils/reader-source-info.ts and searched repository references to projection exports.
Searched duplicated Sanitizable*/ParsedDocument declarations with rg. Did not run tests because the review was read-only inspection.
